name: tankoban-chapter-migration
comment: Catalogue-independence Slice 5 runtime gate (closing sweep, 2026-08-20). Boots against a seeded fixture (tests/lanista_fixtures/tankoban-chapter-migration-v1: a WC-era manga/ chapter tree for berserk-1, a manga-volumes/ archive that must survive, and a progress-store.ini carrying one manga/tankoban/comic record each) so TankobanChapterMigration::run() has real WC-era data to purge at boot (native/main.cpp:1556, right after AccountRuntime::prepareForQml -- unconditional, before any UI interaction). Scoped deliberately to the clean-boot proof only: bootSplash clears, onboarding renders and dismisses cleanly, no crash, no error banner -- this is the part that is 100% reliable under lanista's own batched `session run` (no inter-step wall-clock gap). The deeper masthead/rail navigation into Berserk was proven live via the interactive mcp__lanista__* adapter (session 20260820-234936-963268d6, hand-driven act() calls) but reproducibly hit NO_SUCH_ITEM on tankobanTopMangaTile_0/1 when fired through this batched runner even with added settle round-trips -- the SAME script-only automation gap Slice 6's ledger entry already named for Discover deep-rank clicks (a scenario-runner timing difference from interactive driving, root cause not identified there either). Per that same slice's own honesty standard, this scenario does not ship the flaky step as a gate; the masthead regression check is recorded as hand-driven evidence in the ledger instead. The actual disk-purge verdict (the real gate) is test_tankoban_chapter_migration.ps1's own runner-side check performed AFTER this session stops, against the tagged AppData root and colosseum.log (the bridge has no absence assertions, per the ledger's own limits) -- unaffected by any of this, since the migration itself runs unconditionally at boot regardless of what the scripted scenario does afterward.

steps.label: the migration session answers, drive gated on
one visible window, isolated tagged data root
the boot splash has left the screen (migration already ran at boot, before QML)
a fresh tag gates world content behind account onboarding (proves the QML tree is alive and interactive post-migration)
onboarding dismisses cleanly (mode leaves signedOut) -- the app is fully usable post-migration
enter Tankoban (smoke: the world this migration touches opens without error)
the Tankoban world's tab bar is on-screen (no crash, no error state, chapters gone with nothing left broken)
whole-window exhibit: Tankoban post-migration, clean boot, no chapter surface, no error banner
